answer: In this PoA design, each identity posts bonded collateral, but correlated equivocation across k identities is detected through shared signing patterns and incurs an aggregate penalty proportional to O(k^2), rather than k independent fines. A sybil operator cannot bridge liability across aliases: detection applies an exponential multiplier to capital loss, rapidly exhausting escrowed funds. A mesa of coordinated nodes gains no safety, while an island of isolated identities remains accountable individually.
